# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Denial of ACL Reconstruction (CPT 29888) — Reference Number POC-5D5B151DE3-65694**
**Member:** Rowan Ellison | **Member ID:** W486282210
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-17
**Payer/Plan:** Ambetter (WellCare), Commercial/ACA, North Carolina

To Whom It May Concern:

I am appealing the denial of my ACL reconstruction surgery (CPT 29888), which was denied in the notice dated 2026-08-17 (reference number POC-5D5B151DE3-65694). I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in your possession show that the reason given for the denial does not match my actual treatment history.

## Why I Am Appealing

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I have not been provided with the specific written criteria the plan used to decide what counts as an "adequate trial" of conservative treatment. I understand that musculoskeletal surgery reviews for this plan are handled by TurningPoint, and that TurningPoint's clinical criteria are not published for members to read in advance. I am requesting, in this letter, that the plan provide me in writing the exact criteria that were applied to my case, including the specific policy or guideline document and any citations used to reach this determination. I understand that a plan is required to make available, upon request, the specific criteria relied upon in a denial, and I am making that request formally here.

Because I have not been given the plan's own quoted criteria, I cannot map my records to specific language from the policy. What I can do is lay out, plainly, what my records already show about the conservative treatment I completed before surgery was requested.

## My Treatment History

According to my prior authorization packet and medical records:

- **Symptom duration:** I had 14 months of progressive knee pain that did not improve with rest.
- **Physical therapy:** I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-03-27 through 2026-07-03), totaling 20 visits, focused on range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, along with bracing. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** I used NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief.
- **Injection:** I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-28, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** An MRI of the knee on 2026-07-01 showed a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, with a bone bruise pattern. My menisci were intact and there was no significant arthritis.
- **Function:** I have recurrent instability with pivoting, and my knee has given way twice on stairs.
- **Exam findings:** My exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Other factors:** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

Based on these records, I completed a structured, supervised course of physical therapy, sustained medication trial, and an injection attempt, over more than a year, before my surgeon requested surgery. Without the plan's own written criteria in front of me, I am not able to say precisely which requirement the plan believes was not met — which is exactly why I am asking for that written criteria as part of this appeal.

## What I Am Asking For

1. Please reconsider the denial of CPT 29888 (ACL reconstruction) for date of service [date of service placeholder, if different from authorization request date], in light of the conservative treatment history documented above.
2. Please provide, in writing, the specific clinical review criteria applied to my case, including the name of the policy or guideline document used by TurningPoint or Ambetter (WellCare) in this determination.
3. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and let me know if any additional records are needed to complete your review.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-13, which the plan has stated is 180 days from the date of the denial notice, though I understand the date printed on my denial letter governs. I am submitting this appeal through the Ambetter Health website (ambetterhealth.com), selecting North Carolina and using that state's appeal/grievance form, and/or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and/or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Thank you for your time in reviewing this appeal. I am hopeful that a full review of my records, together with the criteria the plan applied, will support coverage for this surgery.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Rowan Ellison
Member ID: W486282210
[Address placeholder]
[Phone number placeholder]
[Email placeholder]
Date: [date of submission placeholder]

**Enclosures:** Physical therapy discharge note; MRI report dated 2026-07-01; clinic notes from Dr. Okafor; [any additional records placeholder]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
